annotations.title: Daily Agent Signal — one archive day

description: [PAID — 0.04 USDC on Base via x402] Use this when you want the full brief currently stored for one date, for example to review its judgments and sources. Not when you want the most recent stored edition (use signal_latest) or several consecutive days (signal_history, one flat price). ONE stored date's full Signal brief, cheaper than buying full history when you need one date. Returns that date's current stored revision, which can change after publication; it is not an immutable as-of snapshot for backtesting. Check brief.generated_at and brief_sha256 to identify the returned revision. Body { date: YYYY-MM-DD }; only stored dates exist (listed free in /health archive_dates; GET /signal/editions.json, also free, gives each stored edition's headline count, editor pick and the sha256 the paid brief carries, to choose a date), and an unstored date gets a free 404 with payment_taken false, before any payment. $0.04 USDC on Base, paid via x402 by the calling agent's own wallet. Call with no payment_header first to receive the payment requirements; your own wallet pays, never this server's.

date.description: Stored archive date to fetch, format YYYY-MM-DD (one of /health archive_dates). Required.

payment_header.description: Optional. Omit on your first call to receive the x402 payment challenge for free. After your own wallet/x402 client signs against that challenge, call this same tool again with the SAME business arguments plus this field set to the header your x402 client produced (typically { name: "PAYMENT-SIGNATURE", value: "<base64 payload>" }). This server never holds a wallet and never pays on your behalf.

name.description: HTTP header name to attach, e.g. PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.

value.description: HTTP header value (the signed payment payload).
